claims.text: Atom Probe Tomography can reveal oxidation-induced elemental redistribution at nanoprecipitate interfaces.
Atomic-scale compositional changes at nanoprecipitate interfaces have a mechanistic role in the alloy's oxidation behavior.
The as-fabricated additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy contains a uniform distribution of nanoprecipitates.
High-temperature oxidation promotes selective diffusion and segregation of elements at nanoprecipitate/matrix interfaces.
Cr and Ti are examples of elements expected to segregate at nanoprecipitate/matrix interfaces during oxidation.
Interfacial elemental redistribution alters local composition.
Changes in local interfacial composition affect oxidation-scale formation and adherence.
APT can produce three-dimensional atomic-scale elemental maps of the oxidized alloy.
Oxidized samples will exhibit heterogeneous elemental segregation at or near nanoprecipitate interfaces.
The observed redistribution will correlate with regions contributing to enhanced oxidation resistance.
The additively manufactured alloy has enhanced oxidation resistance relative to cast or wrought counterparts.
APT results are limited by spatial resolution and can be influenced by reconstruction artifacts.
APT alone may not quantify each element's effect on oxidation kinetics and scale formation, so complementary TEM-EDS or EELS may be required for validation.
